title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 13th District
area: North-central North Carolina, including Franklin, Harnett, Johnston, and Lee counties and parts of Caswell, Granville, Person, and Wake counties (Raleigh's eastern and northern suburbs, including Clayton, Wake Forest, and Sanford).

context.text: Incumbent Brad Knott defeated one Republican primary challenger with 89.9% of the vote. Paul Barringer won a three-way Democratic primary with 59.1% of the vote.

candidates.name: Brad Knott

summary.text: Brad Knott is the Republican incumbent for North Carolina's 13th Congressional District. A Raleigh native and former federal prosecutor in the Eastern District of North Carolina, he was first elected in 2024 and serves on the Judiciary, Homeland Security, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees. According to his House website, his focus is combating serious crime, economic growth, and defending against threats from within the country's borders.

background.text: Born in Raleigh, North Carolina, in 1986, and attended St. David's School in Raleigh, according to Wikipedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Baylor University and a J.D. from Wake Forest University School of Law.

Worked as a federal prosecutor in the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of North Carolina, from 2016 until November 2023 according to Wikipedia; his House website says he prosecuted organized crime cases including drug cartels, human trafficking, financial crimes and national gangs.

Ran for the 13th District in 2024: finished second in the March 5 Republican primary with 18.7% (behind Kelly Daughtry with 27.4%), won the May 14 runoff with 90.8% after Daughtry unofficially withdrew, and defeated Democrat Frank Pierce 58.6% to 41.4% in November.
Took office in January 2025. According to his House website, he serves in the 119th Congress on the Judiciary, Transportation and Infrastructure, Homeland Security, and Ethics committees.

Committee assignments for the 2025-2026 Congress also include the Homeland Security subcommittees on Border Security and Enforcement and on Oversight, Investigations, and Accountability; the Judiciary subcommittees on Crime and Federal Government Surveillance and on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement; and the Transportation and Infrastructure subcommittees on Aviation, Highways and Transit, and Water Resources and Environment.
His House website says his experience as a prosecutor motivated him to run for office and that he supports robust law enforcement and stronger laws to discourage illegal immigration.
According to his House website, he and his wife, Joanna, are lifelong North Carolinians with two daughters.

priorities.text: Brad's focus in Congress is combatting pervasively serious crime, building an environment for continued economic growth in North Carolina's 13th District and across the nation, and defending against persistent threats to our country from within our own borders.

positions.summary: Sponsor of the Stop Illegal Entry Act, which increases penalties for illegal reentry after deportation and for felonies committed by people in the country illegally, and supported restoring ICE/CBP funding.
positions.quote: As a federal prosecutor, I encountered illegal alien criminals who repeatedly reentered the United States after deportation to continue committing crimes against Americans. This pervasive trend will continue, causing endless harm, unless we implement serious deterrents targeting this class of dangerous criminals.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Homeland Security, the Committee on the Judiciary, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 2025-2026 Congress.

Sponsor of the Stop Illegal Entry Act (with Rep. Stephanie Bice), which passed the House and increases penalties for illegal reentry after deportation and for felonies committed by people in the country illegally.

candidates.name: Paul Barringer
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 59.1% of the vote over two challengers.

summary.text: Paul Barringer is the Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 13th Congressional District. An attorney and health care consultant who grew up in Lee County, he describes more than 20 years working with state governments on Medicaid and other public programs and also manages family timberland. In his Ballotpedia survey he says he is running for independent representation, fiscal responsibility, and practical problem-solving.

background.text: Grew up in Lee County, North Carolina, in the Deep River area near Sanford, and worked for his family's fertilizer company, Sapona Mills, in the 1980s, according to The Rant.

Graduated from Episcopal High School; earned a bachelor's degree in American studies from Davidson College, a law degree from the University of North Carolina, and a master's degree in public affairs from Princeton University.
Describes himself as an attorney and health care consultant with more than 20 years of experience working with state governments to improve Medicaid and other public programs.
Has managed his family's tree farming operation (timberland), practiced as a lawyer, and developed a clothing brand called Mill & Mountain; he also says he provides pro bono legal services.
Says he worked for years in the prison system teaching literacy and helping formerly incarcerated people find employment after release.

According to The Rant, he moved back from the Washington, D.C., area to Lee County in 2025 to be closer to his mother, and decided to run for Congress after becoming concerned about executive orders issued by President Trump in 2025; he said he was registered as a Republican at one point in his life, not long ago.

Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 59.1% of the vote over Frank Pierce and Alexander Nicholi. The Rant reported he is the first major-party congressional nominee from Sanford in recent memory.

priorities.text: Says he is running as an independent voice willing to stand up to any president or wealthy donors, rather than following party leadership.
priorities.quote: I'm running to represent the people of this district – not Donald Trump, party leadership, or billionaire donors. Congress works best when members are willing to stand up to any president who abuses power and to wealthy interests that try to buy influence.

priorities.text: Wants to lower health care costs and strengthen Medicaid oversight, drawing on his background working inside Medicaid and public health systems.
priorities.quote: I've worked inside Medicaid and public health systems and believe meaningful reform will come from better incentives, simplified administration, and collaboration across the system.

priorities.text: Wants to reduce federal spending waste and improve fiscal oversight while lowering health care and education costs.
priorities.quote: Fiscal responsibility means reducing waste, improving oversight, and focusing spending on what actually works.

positions.summary: Supports continued funding for Medicare and Medicaid, saying the market fails to cover seniors, low-income families, and people with disabilities.
positions.quote: The reason we have programs like Medicare and Medicaid in the first place is because the market fails to cover the needs of seniors, low-income families, and those with disabilities. It's our responsibility to continue supporting these vital programs.

positions.summary: Says the law should not stand in the way of a woman's health care decisions made with her doctor, while also supporting expanded maternal health, family planning, and adoption support.
positions.quote: The law should not be an impediment to a woman making the health care choices she needs to make with her doctor.

positions.summary: Describes himself as a responsible gun owner who supports Second Amendment rights, while also supporting enforcement of existing gun laws and bipartisan measures to reduce gun violence.
positions.quote: I believe in the Second Amendment and the right of law-abiding citizens to own firearms, and I also believe we can do more to keep our communities safe.

positions.summary: Supports secure borders and enforcement against illegal crossings and trafficking, alongside modernizing the legal immigration system for workforce needs.
positions.quote: Border security is a basic function of government, and we need smart, effective enforcement to stop illegal crossings, drug trafficking, and exploitation. At the same time, we need to modernize our legal immigration system to meet workforce needs.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, saying they function as a consumer tax that especially hurts farmers, small manufacturers, and rural communities.
positions.quote: Broad tariffs function like a tax on consumers, especially hurting farmers, small manufacturers, and rural communities who rely on affordable materials and access to international markets.

positions.summary: Supports law enforcement having the resources needed to do their jobs, alongside support for rehabilitation and re-entry programs.
positions.quote: I strongly support law enforcement and the vital role police officers play in keeping our communities safe. I believe in ensuring officers have the resources and respect they need to do their jobs.

candidates.name: Anthony Aguilar

summary.text: Anthony Aguilar filed as the Green Party candidate for North Carolina's 13th Congressional District. According to Ballotpedia, he will not appear on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot, and Ballotpedia categorizes him as having withdrawn.

priorities.text: In his campaign launch video, called for an end to US wars.
In his campaign launch video, listed affordable housing among his goals.
In his campaign launch video, said Americans' needs should come first.

candidates.name: Steven Swinton

summary.text: Steven Swinton is the Libertarian Party candidate for North Carolina's 13th Congressional District. Ballotpedia lists no education, occupation or other biographical details for him, and he was the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina Senate District 19 in 2024.

background.text: Was the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina Senate District 19 in 2024, receiving 2,884 of 88,586 votes cast.
Is on the November 3, 2026 ballot for the 13th Congressional District after the Libertarian primary was canceled.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, BallotReady profile, or public policy statements were found for Swinton as of Oct. 19, 2026.
